project: Finding high-Tc superconductors with materials foundation models
summary: Predict Tc for conventional and unconventional superconductors from crystal structure, screen open databases for high-Tc candidates, and probe what the models learn about pairing mechanisms.

stages.name: Direction and plan
stages.detail: Machine learning for superconductors with open materials foundation models

stages.name: Compute environment
stages.detail: Training runs on GitHub Actions; setting up this repository and the desktop app

stages.name: Electron–phonon data
stages.detail: 7,582 Alexandria entries kept for training (of 8,253); 1,032 JARVIS entries held out as the locked test set; Tc recomputed with mu* = 0.1

stages.name: Measured-Tc data, including unconventional
stages.detail: Experimental Tc for cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion and other families from SuperCon-derived datasets with crystal structures

stages.name: Baseline models
stages.detail: Electron-phonon baseline done (gradient boosting, composition + structure features); measured-Tc baseline next

stages.name: Foundation-model descriptors + prediction heads
stages.detail: Frozen MACE-MP-0 descriptors, one head per track, ensembles for uncertainty

stages.name: Locked evaluation
stages.detail: 626 dynamically stable JARVIS materials for electron–phonon; leave-one-family-out tests for unconventional families

stages.name: High-Tc screening
stages.detail: Score candidate structures from open databases; shortlist high predicted Tc with low uncertainty for DFT or experimental follow-up

stages.name: Public v0.1
stages.detail: Code, models, results and the candidate shortlist published on GitHub

stages.name: Mechanism analysis
stages.detail: Compare electron–phonon Tc with measured Tc to flag materials phonons can't explain, and test known structure–Tc correlations within families
